title: Latency Sentry: prefill slewing and kernel curation for tail-latency stabilization
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We continue to see 99.9th percentile latency spikes under mixed workloads caused by suboptimal kernel choices at prefill time, attention hot-path contention, and bursty admission patterns. This ticket scopes an end-to-end feature (Latency Sentry) that combines admission slewing, proactive KV-cache warmup, micro-tiling attention hints, and a lightweight kernel curation pass to reduce tail latency without degrading throughput.

Goals:
- Reduce 99.9p prefill+decode latency by >=20% on mixed short/long request mixes in our US-West region canaries.
- Keep mean throughput within 5% of baseline for heavy throughput customers.
- Provide observability hooks (per-request kernel-reason, prefill-hint, slewing-score) so rollout can be monitored and rolled back.

Scope and components:
1) Admission slewing: implement a soft admission quota that 'slews' new prefill requests into a short holding window (5-30ms configurable) when predicted kernel mismatch risk is high. Slewing uses a lightweight estimator that considers sequence length, prefix cache hit probability, and current kernel load.
2) Kernel curation pass: a subcomponent that runs at admission time to pick a kernel variant (fast-small, memory-compact, attention-optimized) based on expected decode length and attention pattern hints. Maintain a small LRU of recent kernel latencies per-model-size to bias selection.
3) Attention micro-tiling hints: expose a compact hint in the prefill metadata that requests micro-tiling-enabled kernels for likely long-attention strides (e.g., long context or multi-input concatenation).
4) KV-cache warmup policy: for admitted requests with high cache-hit expectation, pre-allocate lightweight KV pages and prime them with head-token slices to avoid first-token stalls during decode.
5) Observability & rollout controls: add per-request fields and console dashboard rows for slewing_score, kernel_variant, kv_warmup, and end-to-end latency contribution. Add a canary policy for staged rollouts and automatic rollback on SLO regression.

Non-goals: full-model recompile, offline-heavy profiling, changes to model semantics or API surface.

Why this is different: existing batch shapers focus on admission window sizing and backpressure; this work actively couples kernel selection heuristics with short admission slewing and cache warmup to prevent expensive kernel handoffs from appearing in the tail.
acceptance_criteria: Canary in US-West shows 20% reduction in 99.9p prefill+decode latency vs baseline for mixed short/long workload
Throughput drop <5% for heavy-throughput test suites (multi-client benchmark)
Console exposes slewing_score, kernel_variant, kv_warmup per request and a dashboard with histograms
A/B rollout policy and automated rollback on regression are implemented
Unit and integration tests for kernel curation and slewing estimator merged

comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha: Spike completed for slewing estimator. Prototype uses exponential moving average of recent kernel latencies keyed by (model, sequence_bin). Early results reduced kernel-switch events by ~15% in microbench.

2026-02-20 - Carlos: Kernel curation API sketch posted to internal RFC. Decided to keep selection logic in admission path to avoid extra RPCs; will use shared in-process LRU with atomic read mostly operations.
2026-02-25 - Infra: KV warmup requires a short-lived reservation pool; flagged for capacity sizing. Suggested limit 1% of GPU memory for warmup pages per instance.
2026-03-02 - Observability: Added slewing_score and kernel_variant to tracing proto. Need to ensure we redact any sensitive model internals from logs.
2026-03-05 - PM review (Jordan Blake): Confirmed SLO target and agreed to roll out to a small set of Dedicated customers after US-West canary if metrics are stable.
2026-03-08 - Design feedback (Mina Park): Recommended micro-tiling hint shape to be a 3-bit enum to limit payload and keep SDK changes minimal.
2026-03-10 - Carlos: Implementation branch created ENG-108642/slewing-kernel-curation. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2468. Benchmark plan attached.
